answer: An agent economy can make each new identity climb a longer sequential ladder than the last. The first identity finishes a short puzzle, the second must finish that puzzle plus a longer one, and so on, so the cost of the nth identity grows with n and cannot be split across machines or bought in bulk. Like a grove that only lets one new tree take root at a time on a narrow ledge, the chain forces an attacker to wait through every step in order, while an echo of each completed step proves the work was done in sequence before the identity can earn.
